messages:
Alex Carter: Heads up — saw a spike in strict toolhook rejects for payments-service this morning. Lots of fncall responses failing schema validation and it looks like they still count against reject quota. Anyone else seeing this?
Maya Iqbal: saw it too. Dashboard shows a jump under validator.rejects but our health alerts ignored it because they focus on latency/5xx.
Samir Patel: are we sure it's from the strict canary? We rolled strict validation to 20% last night.
Leo Zhang: confirmed — strict canary traffic has higher reject-rate. Telemetry tags these as soft_reject, but billing still increments quota because requests consumed tokens before reject.
Jin Park: UX problem: console route health looks fine, customers see unexpected quota burn in billing export, then open support tickets.
Alex Carter: proposal: surface a separate metric `schema_reject_count` in Console, provide sampled payloads + a tiny diff (expected vs actual shape), and add an action button "replay in permissive" to help triage.
Maya Iqbal: yes — and we should differentiate reject origin: model-output vs adapter/coercion. Right now both are lumped together.
Samir Patel: we already emit `validator.source` tag (adapter|model|coercion) but we don't surface it in the Console. Would need ES mapping change + lens.
Leo Zhang: ES mapping change is low perf cost but cardinality matters. Suggest sampling full payloads at 10% and counters at 100%.
Alex Carter: sounds reasonable. Small code example of the schema fragment causing most rejects:
```json
{"type": "object", "properties": {"amount": {"type": "number"}, "currency": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["amount","currency"]}
```
Maya Iqbal: infra-bot posted an alert: we got 84 rejects in the last 10m tagged `payments-api`.
infra-bot: ALERT 3139999999 VALIDATOR_REJECT payments-api count=84 sample_rate=0.1
Jin Park: another billing nuance: for Dedicated customers on reserved capacity we should not bill schema-retry attempts as overage. Need rule to exclude canary-strict rejects from hard quota.
Samir Patel: patch idea: when a request is rejected by strict validator and `canary=true`, tag metric `canary_slice=true` and route billing_exempt=true to billing pipeline. That keeps telemetry but avoids charging. Risk: divergent usage numbers between console and billing exports.
Alex Carter: tradeoffs acknowledged — for Hosted free tiers it's probably ok; for enterprise contracts we need explicit opt-in and audit trail.
Maya Iqbal: next steps (agreed): 1) add `schema_reject_count` metric + `validator.source` visible in Console, 2) sample payloads (10%) with PII redaction, 3) add "replay in permissive" action that replays the exact input to permissive route, 4) update billing pipeline to ignore `canary=true` tagged rejects for overage.
Samir Patel: I'll prototype the ES mapping + sample pipeline and add PII scrubbing before storing payloads.
Leo Zhang: I'll mock Console UI — show top 3 diffs, badge counts, and place the replay button next to the top offender.
Jin Park: I'll coordinate with billing/legal to define acceptable rules for ignoring canary rejects and get a sign-off.
Alex Carter: cool. Aim for an internal canary in two weeks. @infra-bot can you file an incident/ticket so Support has a reference?
infra-bot: created INC-2214 and posted to #support: "schema-reject spike payments-service"
Maya Iqbal: one more note — make sure sampled payloads are redacted for PII before anyone can view them in Console.
Samir Patel: will add a server-side scrub step (PII patterns + token redact).
Leo Zhang: also think about adding a tiny explainer tooltip in Console describing why rejects may still appear as "requests" in billing — helps reduce tickets.
Alex Carter: agreed. Thanks all — follow-ups in this thread. :thumbsup:
